subject: pe
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A bar chart is most appropriate for comparing:
options: Separate categories such as scores for different teams
questions.explain: Bar charts are best for comparing values across separate, discrete categories.

questions.q: Quantitative data is best described as:
options: Numerical data that can be measured
Data based on opinions and feelings
questions.explain: Quantitative data is objective and numerical, such as times, scores or heart rate.

questions.q: A coach's written opinion on a player's effort is an example of:
questions.explain: Qualitative data is descriptive and based on opinions, judgements or observations.

questions.q: Which type of chart is most suitable for showing how heart rate changes continuously over time?
questions.explain: A line graph best shows continuous change over time, such as heart rate during exercise.

questions.q: A 20-year-old wants to train at 70% of their maximum heart rate. What is the target heart rate?
Why is it useful to collect data when analysing performance?
options: It gives objective evidence to identify strengths and weaknesses
It replaces the need for skill
questions.explain: Data provides objective evidence to identify strengths and weaknesses and to set targets.

questions.q: What is the maximum heart rate of a 15-year-old using the standard formula?
questions.explain: Maximum heart rate is estimated as 220 - age, so 220 - 15 = 205 bpm.

questions.q: Which is an advantage of quantitative over qualitative data?
options: It is based on personal opinion
It is easy to compare and analyse objectively
questions.explain: Quantitative data is numerical and objective, making it easier to compare and analyse reliably.

questions.q: On a graph of heart rate during exercise, a sharp rise at the start most likely shows:
options: The anticipatory rise and onset of exercise
questions.explain: Heart rate rises sharply at the start of exercise (and even just before it) to meet the increased demand for oxygen.

questions.q: If a graph shows heart rate returning slowly to resting after exercise, this section represents:
questions.explain: After exercise the heart rate gradually falls back to resting during the recovery period.

questions.q: How would you calculate a 40-year-old's estimated maximum heart rate?
questions.explain: Maximum heart rate is estimated as 220 - age, so 220 - 40 = 180 bpm.

questions.q: A pie chart is most useful for showing:
options: Proportions of a whole, such as percentage of training time per method
Change in heart rate over time
questions.explain: Pie charts show how a whole is divided into proportions or percentages.
